paragraphs: This paper searches for synaptic learning rules by asking what a network should become after learning. Existing plasticity models often fit biological observations without producing useful network functions. The authors instead constrain candidate rules through the functions and structures they should produce, using meta-learning to search for plausible solutions.

They express plasticity rules through a Volterra expansion and optimize their parameters using gradient descent or evolutionary strategies. A task-specific loss measures how effectively each rule turns an initially random network into one that performs the desired function. The learned object is therefore the rule governing network change.

The framework rediscovers Oja’s rule for extracting the principal direction of input variation, then finds rules that recover several principal components at the network level. In integrate-and-fire networks, it also discovers a subset of inhibitory plasticity rules that achieve a target firing rate against tuned excitation. These results establish a proof of principle for discovering functionally useful rules under biological constraints, rather than identifying a unique biological learning mechanism.
neurips-2020-a-meta-learning-approach-to.tldr: Meta-learning discovers plausible synaptic plasticity rules by optimizing the network functions those rules produce.

paragraphs: Attention modules determine how a model distributes emphasis across available information. Most use deterministic weights because they are straightforward to train. This paper develops stochastic attention modules that preserve practical optimization while allowing attention weights to come from learned probability distributions.

The construction starts with distributions that support reparameterization, allowing their sampling process to participate in differentiable training. Normalization turns the resulting values into attention weights constrained to sum to one. The authors learn the distribution parameters within a Bayesian framework and introduce a data-dependent prior to regularize them. This addresses a central obstacle to stochastic attention: incorporating randomness without making optimization unwieldy.

The modules are applied to graph node classification, visual question answering, image captioning, machine translation, and language understanding. Across the reported experiments, they consistently improve on the corresponding baseline models. The contribution is thus both a distributional formulation of attention and a practical way to incorporate it into several existing attention-based architectures. The empirical findings support its usefulness across the tested applications.
neurips-2020-bayesian-attention-modules-.tldr: Bayesian attention modules make stochastic attention differentiable and practical, with consistent improvements across the tested applications.

paragraphs: Bongard-LOGO tests whether a system can infer visual concepts from a few examples and apply them beyond those examples. The motivation is a gap between strong performance on data-rich recognition tasks and the flexible concept learning people display. The benchmark extends the challenge posed by the original Bongard problems.

The authors use programs in the action-oriented LOGO language to generate a large collection of human-interpretable visual reasoning problems. The design emphasizes three capabilities: interpreting an object differently depending on context, shifting between meaningful concepts when making analogies, and learning from few examples without restricting concepts to a fixed vocabulary. Program-guided generation provides a way to build many problems around these demands.

In the reported experiments, state-of-the-art deep learning methods perform substantially worse than human participants. The authors interpret this gap as evidence that the tested methods do not capture the targeted properties of human cognition. The benchmark makes those shortcomings measurable and motivates research toward a more general architecture for visual reasoning.
neurips-2020-bongard-logo-a-new-benchmar.tldr: Bongard-LOGO exposes a substantial gap between tested deep learning methods and humans on visual concept learning from few examples.

paragraphs: Generalization bounds describe how learning from a training set relates to performance beyond that set. Information-theoretic approaches study this relationship through mutual information between the learned model and its training data. This paper develops a graphical framework for improving such bounds and understanding connections among existing results.

The authors represent the relevant random variables and their dependencies using a probabilistic graph. They introduce two operations on this representation. Conditioning treats a selected variable as given. Processing replaces a variable with one of its children in the graph. These operations provide systematic ways to change the information quantities used in an analysis.

The improvements can take two forms: a tighter bound or a bound applicable in more situations. The paper shows that the framework offers a unified explanation for several recent tightening results and uses it to derive new improved bounds. Its significance lies in organizing apparently separate advances around a shared set of techniques, while also supplying tools for developing further generalization analyses.
neurips-2020-conditioning-and-processing.tldr: Conditioning and processing provide a graphical framework for tightening information-theoretic generalization bounds or broadening their applicability.

paragraphs: This paper introduces Contracting-domain Newton methods for composite convex optimization. These algorithms use second-order information to build global lower approximations of the smooth part of an objective. Such approximations connect the local curvature information used by Newton-style methods with a global approach to reducing the objective.

The methods are affine-invariant, meaning their formulation respects affine changes of coordinates. The authors give two complementary interpretations: a second-order extension of conditional gradient methods and a variant of a trust-region scheme. These interpretations situate the approach within familiar optimization strategies while explaining how curvature enters the update process.

For a bounded problem domain and convex functions with a Lipschitz-continuous Hessian, the authors prove that the objective-value gap decreases at a rate of O(1/k²), where k counts iterations. This improves the previously known O(1/k) bound for this type of algorithm. The paper also proposes a stochastic extension and reports computations for empirical risk minimization. The faster theoretical rate is explicitly tied to the stated domain and smoothness conditions.
neurips-2020-convex-optimization-based-o.tldr: Contracting-domain Newton methods achieve an O(1/k²) objective-gap rate under bounded-domain and Hessian-smoothness assumptions.

paragraphs: Cross-validation provides an estimate of test error, but interpreting that estimate also requires understanding its uncertainty. This paper develops a theoretical basis for confidence intervals around k-fold test error and for testing whether one learning algorithm has lower k-fold test error than another.

The authors establish central limit theorems under weak stability conditions on the learning algorithm. They also construct consistent estimates of the asymptotic variance, the quantity needed to translate the limiting distribution into usable uncertainty estimates. Together, these results yield confidence intervals whose coverage becomes exact asymptotically, along with valid and powerful comparison tests. The guarantee concerns large-sample behavior under the stated stability conditions.

The results also cover leave-one-out cross-validation, for which the authors report the first results of this kind. In experiments spanning diverse learning algorithms, the proposed intervals and tests outperform popular alternatives from the literature. The practical contribution is a principled way to attach uncertainty to cross-validation estimates and assess whether observed differences between algorithms are statistically supported.
neurips-2020-cross-validation-confidence.tldr: Under weak stability conditions, cross-validation supports asymptotically exact confidence intervals and principled tests comparing learning algorithms.

paragraphs: Text-based games require an agent to make decisions in an environment described through natural language. Representing the text and possible actions is only part of that problem: the agent also needs to use relationships in its knowledge to support decisions. This paper addresses that reasoning component within reinforcement learning.

The proposed method uses knowledge graphs and a stacked hierarchical attention mechanism. By exploiting the graph’s structure, the attention mechanism constructs an explicit representation of the reasoning process. The aim is for an action to be supported by an interpretable inference procedure, connecting what the agent knows with the choice it makes.

The authors evaluate the approach extensively on human-made benchmark games and report better performance than existing text-based agents. These findings support the value of incorporating structured reasoning into the tested game-playing systems. The contribution combines a decision-making architecture with an explicit account of its reasoning, making the graph structure useful both for selecting actions and for representing how those actions are supported.
neurips-2020-deep-reinforcement-learning.tldr: Stacked hierarchical attention uses knowledge graphs to support interpretable reasoning and improves performance on tested text-based games.

paragraphs: Vector graphics describe images through shapes and drawing commands, allowing them to scale across display resolutions. DeepSVG learns representations of this structured format and uses them to generate and interpolate complex SVG icons. The paper addresses a form of image modeling that had received less attention than learning from raster images.

Its hierarchical network separates the high-level organization of shapes from the low-level commands that describe each shape. The network predicts a set of shapes directly in a non-autoregressive manner. This organization gives the model a way to handle both the composition of an icon and the detailed instructions defining its constituent shapes.

The authors introduce a large-scale dataset for complex SVG icon generation and an open-source library for manipulating SVGs. They demonstrate accurate reconstruction of diverse vector graphics and show how interpolation and other operations in the learned latent space can support animation. The results connect representation learning with practical graphics manipulation: a learned representation can serve as a space in which vector designs are transformed.
neurips-2020-deepsvg-a-hierarchical-gene.tldr: DeepSVG separates shapes from drawing commands to learn vector representations that support icon generation, reconstruction, and animation.

paragraphs: An intervention can vary continuously, as when a treatment has an adjustable dosage. Estimating its effect therefore requires more than comparing a few discrete treatment choices. This paper introduces SCIGAN, a modified generative adversarial framework for estimating counterfactual outcomes across several different continuous interventions using observational data.

SCIGAN first learns to generate counterfactual outcomes. Those generated outcomes then support training an inference model through standard supervised learning, enabling predictions for new samples. A central architectural contribution is a hierarchical discriminator designed around the structure of continuous interventions. The discriminator adapts the adversarial learning process to the setting the model needs to handle.

The authors provide theoretical results supporting both the GAN formulation and the hierarchical discriminator. They also introduce a semi-synthetic data simulation for continuous interventions and report improvements over existing benchmark models. The contribution is a route from generated counterfactual outcomes to a reusable prediction model, together with theoretical support and experimental evidence in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2020-estimating-the-effects-of-c.tldr: SCIGAN uses a modified GAN and hierarchical discriminator to estimate counterfactual outcomes for multiple continuously varying interventions.

paragraphs: Adding Gaussian noise during neural network training can change which functions the network learns. This paper examines that regularizing effect when noise is injected into network activations. Its focus is on explaining the mathematical preference introduced by this practice, an aspect less studied than adding noise directly to training data.

The authors derive an explicit regularizer by averaging over the injected noise. This makes the effect of random perturbations expressible as a penalty on the learned function. In the Fourier domain, the penalty discourages high-frequency components, which describe rapidly varying aspects of a function. The effect is particularly pronounced in layers closer to the network’s output.

The paper connects this regularization to classification behavior through both analysis and experiments. It reports calibrated classifiers with large classification margins. Calibration concerns how well predictive confidence reflects correctness, while margins describe separation in classification decisions. These findings give a concrete interpretation to activation noise: its influence includes a preference against rapid functional variation, with demonstrated consequences for confidence and decision separation.
neurips-2020-explicit-regularisation-in-.tldr: Gaussian activation noise induces a penalty on high-frequency functions and is linked analytically and empirically to calibrated, large-margin classifiers.

paragraphs: Continual learning becomes difficult when earlier datasets are no longer accessible. This paper approaches that problem by retaining information through a generative memory: a system that can produce data associated with datasets encountered over time. Its motivation is that perfectly retained data information would remove the corresponding cause of forgetting.

The proposed GAN memory builds on a well-behaved base GAN. The authors observe that changing its style can produce perceptually distant target distributions, and use sequential style modulations to form generators for successive datasets. This process also transfers knowledge from the base model, so learning later generative targets can benefit from information already available.

The paper describes the resulting memory as retaining a stream of datasets without forgetting. Its classification experiments support the more specific downstream claim that the approach alleviates catastrophic forgetting, and the reported comparisons favor it over existing approaches. The distinction matters: preserving generative memories supplies information for continual classification, while the stated classification result is an improvement in forgetting behavior.
neurips-2020-gan-memory-with-no-forgetti.tldr: Sequential style modulation creates a GAN memory described as retaining past datasets without forgetting and empirically alleviates forgetting in continual classification.

paragraphs: Gaussian Gated Linear Networks extend a neural network family whose learning process uses local credit assignment. In gated linear networks, components optimize convex objectives rather than learning features through backpropagation. The paper builds on this approach to handle regression and probability density modeling in addition to classification.

The central change generalizes geometric mixing into a product of Gaussian densities. This gives the framework a way to combine continuous probability distributions and produce predictions for one or multiple output variables. The broader GLN framework is associated with universality, efficient online learning, interpretability, and robustness to catastrophic forgetting; the proposed extension brings its learning approach to these additional prediction settings.

On several univariate and multivariate regression benchmarks, G-GLN achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance. The authors also demonstrate applications to online contextual bandits and density estimation through denoising. These results show that local, convex learning mechanisms can support a range of continuous prediction tasks, with practical evidence extending beyond conventional regression benchmarks.
neurips-2020-gaussian-gated-linear-netwo.tldr: Gaussian Gated Linear Networks extend local convex learning to regression and density modeling by combining Gaussian distributions.

paragraphs: Large neural networks can contain substantial redundancy, making it possible to remove parts while retaining useful behavior. The theoretical question is how the size of a reduced network relates to its deviation from the original. This paper proposes a greedy optimization method for pruning and provides a quantitative answer to that relationship.

Under assumptions the authors describe as weak and applicable to most practical settings, the discrepancy between the pruned and original networks decreases exponentially as the pruned network grows. This gives a principled connection between the amount of retained capacity and approximation quality. The statement concerns discrepancy from the original network and is conditional on the assumptions.

The empirical evaluation covers several architectures, including ResNet and MobileNetV2/V3 on ImageNet. The authors report improvements over prior pruning methods in these experiments. Together, the theoretical and empirical results support greedy pruning as a way to obtain smaller networks while controlling deviation from their originals, with the theory explaining how approximation quality can improve as more capacity is retained.
neurips-2020-greedy-optimization-provabl.tldr: A greedy pruning method has conditional exponential discrepancy guarantees and improves on prior pruning approaches in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Recordings from many electrodes can reveal relationships between brain regions, but strong correlations within a region may obscure the relationships of interest. LDFA-H analyzes high-dimensional time series through latent factors, aiming to extract cross-region dynamics from measurements containing substantial within-region noise correlation.

The method combines a new estimator of the covariance structure among observed time series with a dynamic extension of probabilistic canonical correlation analysis for latent variables. The focus is on cross-correlations among those latent variables. In neural data, these relationships may reflect information flowing between brain regions, although the interpretation remains a possibility rather than a direct causal conclusion.

In simulations, LDFA-H captures target factors even when noise-related within-region correlation dominates cross-region correlation, outperforming existing methods in that respect. The authors also analyze local field potentials from 192 electrodes in prefrontal cortex and visual area V4 during a memory-guided saccade task. The results reveal changing lead-lag dependencies between the regions and show where the associated signals are distributed spatially.
neurips-2020-latent-dynamic-factor-analy.tldr: LDFA-H extracts latent cross-region dynamics from high-dimensional neural recordings, including when within-region noise correlations dominate.

paragraphs: Graph classification becomes harder when new node labels appear with only a few examples. MetaTNE addresses this combination of novelty and scarce supervision. An example is recognizing a newly formed group in a social network when only a handful of its members are available as labeled training nodes.

The framework has three modules. A structural module embeds nodes according to graph structure. A meta-learning module learns prior knowledge about relationships between structure and labels, then uses that knowledge to help learn new labels. An embedding transformation function addresses shortcomings of applying meta-learning directly. Finally, an optimization module schedules training to balance structural learning with meta-learning.

Experiments on four real-world datasets show large improvements over state-of-the-art methods. The approach matters because graph structure supplies information beyond the few labeled examples, while meta-learning captures experience that can be reused when unfamiliar labels arrive. The transformation and training schedule organize how these sources of information contribute, and the reported results support the complete framework in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2020-node-classification-on-grap.tldr: MetaTNE combines graph embeddings, meta-learning, and embedding transformation to classify newly emerging labels from few examples.

paragraphs: This paper uses a single neural network to approximate solutions across a parameterized family of high-dimensional linear Kolmogorov equations. The objective includes variation across equation parameters as well as space and time. Learning the family together provides a common representation of solutions throughout a full space-time region.

The method uses the Feynman-Kac formula to reformulate numerical approximation of the whole equation family as one statistical learning problem. Training uses simulated data. This reformulation makes it possible to apply deep learning to a collection of related differential equations through a shared prediction task.

The authors report successful experiments on heat equations and Black-Scholes option pricing models parameterized by affine-linear coefficient functions. These experiments support the algorithm’s functionality and efficiency and demonstrate learning an entire family with one network. The paper also presents numerical observations and theoretical results showing that the proposed method avoids the curse of dimensionality in its studied setting. That claim concerns this approach to the specified equation families, rather than arbitrary differential equations.
neurips-2020-numerically-solving-paramet.tldr: A Feynman-Kac learning formulation lets one neural network approximate entire families of high-dimensional Kolmogorov equation solutions.

paragraphs: This paper studies learning Ising models when some observed samples may be corrupted arbitrarily. The goal is to estimate the underlying model reliably despite that contamination. The analysis allows the model to grow with the amount of data: the numbers of nodes and edges, and the maximum node degree, can all increase with sample size.

The proposed estimators exploit moments of the underlying distribution and reduce parts of the problem to estimation of a single variable. These reductions connect a high-dimensional robust learning problem to simpler estimation tasks. The resulting analysis tracks both the effect of corrupted observations and the amount of data needed for accurate estimation.

The estimators achieve optimal dependence on the corrupted fraction that does not worsen with dimension. They simultaneously provide high-probability error guarantees with optimal sample complexity. Dimension independence applies specifically to the contamination dependence; the abstract does not characterize every part of the estimation problem that way. Simulations corroborate the theory, supporting the proposed approach to learning growing Ising models from contaminated samples.
neurips-2020-on-learning-ising-models-un.tldr: Moment-based estimators learn contaminated Ising models with optimal, dimension-independent contamination dependence and optimal sample complexity.

paragraphs: A continual learner must adapt to new tasks while preserving access to earlier knowledge. OSAKA brings these demands together in a scenario requiring rapid learning of out-of-distribution tasks and rapid remembering of previous ones. It builds on two research directions that combine meta-learning with continual learning in different ways.

One direction uses meta-learning before continual learning to reduce forgetting. The other trains agents to recover previous tasks quickly through adaptation. The authors argue that their original formulations have limitations and propose OSAKA as a more general setting. In their study, existing continual learning, meta-learning, and combined approaches fail to meet the demands of this scenario.

The paper introduces Continual-MAML, an online extension of MAML, as a strong baseline. Empirical comparisons find it better suited to OSAKA than the evaluated alternatives. The contribution therefore includes both a setting that tests adaptation and remembering together and an algorithm designed for those combined demands. The reported advantage establishes empirical suitability for this scenario rather than a universal solution to continual learning.
neurips-2020-online-fast-adaptation-and-.tldr: OSAKA tests rapid adaptation and remembering together, with Continual-MAML providing a stronger empirical baseline than the evaluated alternatives.

paragraphs: Training with an importance-weighted variational bound requires estimating gradients from samples. Increasing the number of samples can change how much useful signal those estimates contain relative to noise. This paper studies that relationship for score-function estimators and develops a way to reduce their variance.

The authors prove that, as the number of importance samples K becomes large, a suitable control variate can make the signal-to-noise ratio grow as the square root of K. For the standard pathwise gradient estimator, the corresponding ratio instead decreases as the inverse square root of K. The favorable result depends on choosing the control variate appropriately and is an asymptotic statement.

Guided by the theory, the paper develops a control variate extending VIMCO. In experiments with continuous and discrete generative models, it provides superior variance reduction and a signal-to-noise ratio that increases with K without reparameterization. The estimator is also competitive with Reweighted Wake-Sleep and the thermodynamic variational objective. The findings show how variance control can make additional importance samples useful for reparameterization-free gradient estimation.
neurips-2020-optimal-variance-control-of.tldr: An appropriately chosen control variate can make score-function gradient signal-to-noise improve with more importance samples.

paragraphs: Path Integral Based Graph Neural Networks, or PAN, use paths through a graph to define how nodes exchange information. The framework addresses both convolution, which combines information, and pooling, which reduces the graph representation. It is designed for classification and regression on graphs with different sizes and structures.

The convolution considers every path connecting a sender and receiver, with learned weights depending on path length. Drawing on a path-integral formulation, the authors derive a maximal entropy transition matrix associated with maximal entropy random walks. Its diagonal entries relate directly to subgraph centrality, providing a natural basis for adaptive pooling within the same framework.

The authors present PAN as a broad formulation in which most existing GNN architectures can be viewed as special cases. Experiments report state-of-the-art results on various graph classification and regression tasks. The paper also introduces a statistical-mechanics benchmark to encourage physical-science applications. Its central contribution is a shared mathematical construction linking how graph information is propagated with how graph structure is pooled.
neurips-2020-path-integral-based-convolu.tldr: PAN derives graph convolution and adaptive pooling from a path-based transition matrix, achieving strong results on tested graph tasks.

paragraphs: Deep density models can learn by transforming observations into representations with a simple joint distribution. Maximum-likelihood training then involves the log-determinant of the transformation’s Jacobian. Computing with this term can be expensive, creating a tension between flexible transformations and manageable training cost.

This paper proposes an exact training approach based on relative gradients. It exploits the matrix structure of neural network parameters to compute updates efficiently, including in high-dimensional spaces. The reported computational scaling is quadratic in input size, compared with the cubic scaling of naive approaches. This targets a central computational burden of the learning objective.

The approach allows training with the Jacobian log-determinant without imposing structural constraints on the Jacobian. The authors contrast this with autoregressive normalizing flows, whose structure is restricted. The significance is a way to reduce the computational cost of exact training while retaining greater structural freedom in the transformation. The paper also connects the representation-learning objective to nonlinear independent component analysis through its use of simple, factorized representation distributions.
neurips-2020-relative-gradient-optimizat.tldr: Relative gradients enable exact Jacobian-based density-model training with quadratic input-size scaling and without constraining Jacobian structure.

paragraphs: This paper analyzes how gradient-noise distributions affect stochastic gradient descent on smooth, non-convex objectives. Its convergence target is a small squared gradient norm. The analysis therefore concerns reaching approximate stationary behavior, and studies how quickly that happens with high probability under different kinds of noise.

For centered sub-Gaussian noise, the authors prove an iteration bound of O(ε⁻² log(1/δ)) to reach squared-gradient precision ε with probability 1−δ. For centered, integrable heavy-tailed noise, they obtain O(ε⁻ᵖδ⁻ᑫ), with p and q greater than two. Convergence thus remains possible even with unbounded noise variance, although the dependence on accuracy and confidence becomes worse.

Both results follow from a unified analysis using biased expectations, a tool for deriving concentration inequalities. The framework also introduces a measure of gradient noise. The authors identify a step-size scaling proportional to T⁻¹ᐟᵇ, where b is the noise-tail parameter, as yielding the best rates in their analysis. The findings establish a qualified robustness result: the specified heavy-tailed noise slows convergence without preventing it.
neurips-2020-robustness-analysis-of-non-.tldr: A unified analysis shows that centered, integrable heavy-tailed gradient noise can slow SGD convergence without preventing small gradient norms.

paragraphs: This paper learns visual features by first teaching a system a basic ability to group image regions. A contour detector partitions an image, and those regions are merged into a tree hierarchy. A small supervised dataset is sufficient to train this initial grouping component, which then supplies guidance for learning from much more unlabeled data.

Across the unlabeled dataset, the grouping system predicts hierarchical region structure automatically. A deep network learns a representation for each pixel through contrastive learning. Distances between these pixel representations are trained to respect the predicted region hierarchy, connecting the learned feature space to relationships among image regions.

Experiments show that the approach can provide state-of-the-art generic pre-training that benefits downstream tasks. The authors also explore semantic region search and tracking individual objects in video. The contribution is a way to turn limited supervision for a primitive visual task into extensive training guidance. Its self-supervised stage relies on automatically predicted structure, while the initial grouping primitive is explicitly learned with supervision.
neurips-2020-self-supervised-visual-repr.tldr: A grouping primitive trained with limited supervision generates hierarchical guidance for self-supervised pixel representation learning.

paragraphs: This paper studies episodic decision-making when state-transition rules are known but loss feedback is limited to bandit feedback. The goal is an algorithm that performs especially well when losses are stochastic while retaining guarantees when losses are adversarial. These demands are combined in one best-of-both-worlds result.

The algorithm achieves O(log T) regret for stochastic losses and a worst-case regret bound of roughly O(√T), with logarithmic factors suppressed, for adversarial losses. Here T is the number of episodes. For an intermediate setting with total loss corruption C, the authors give a bound expressed as roughly O(√C), again suppressing logarithmic factors. These guarantees connect performance to the loss regime.

The method uses Follow-the-Regularized-Leader with a new hybrid regularizer. Its Hessian is non-diagonal and has a complicated inverse, making the analysis challenging. The central technical contribution is analyzing this regularizer and deriving a particular self-bounding regret guarantee. The results establish adaptability across loss conditions within the specified setting of known transitions and bandit feedback.
neurips-2020-simultaneously-learning-sto.tldr: One episodic MDP algorithm combines logarithmic stochastic regret with adversarial robustness when transitions are known.

paragraphs: Normalizing flows use invertible transformations between variables of the same dimension. This creates a difficulty when the data lie on a manifold whose dimension differs from that of the distribution used by the flow. SoftFlow changes the learning problem to address that mismatch.

Instead of fitting the original data distribution directly, SoftFlow estimates a conditional distribution of perturbed input data. This probabilistic reformulation sidesteps the dimensionality problem while retaining a flow-based generative approach. In the reported experiments, it captures the underlying structure of manifold data and generates high-quality samples, unlike the conventional flow models used in those comparisons.

The authors also apply the framework to three-dimensional point clouds through SoftPointFlow. Thin structures are difficult for flow-based point-cloud models to form, and the proposed approach alleviates that difficulty. It estimates distributions of various shapes more accurately and achieves state-of-the-art point-cloud generation performance in the reported evaluation. The broader contribution is a training framework tailored to data whose intrinsic structure does not match the flow’s ambient dimensionality.
neurips-2020-softflow-probabilistic-fram.tldr: SoftFlow learns conditional distributions of perturbed data to address dimensional mismatch in flows and improve manifold and point-cloud generation.
